biomarkers.name: EGFR
biomarkers.summary: EGFR is widely recognized for its importance in cancer. Amplification and mutations have been shown to be driving events in many cancer types. Its role in non-small cell lung cancer, glioblastoma and basal-like breast cancers has spurred many research and drug development efforts. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors have shown efficacy in EGFR amplfied tumors, most notably gefitinib and erlotinib. Mutations in EGFR have been shown to confer resistance to these drugs, particularly the variant T790M, which has been functionally characterized as a resistance marker for both of these drugs. The later generation TKI's have seen some success in treating these resistant cases, and targeted sequencing of th…

genes.name: EGFR
genes.description: EGFR is widely recognized for its importance in cancer. Amplification and mutations have been shown to be driving events in many cancer types. Its role in non-small cell lung cancer, glioblastoma and basal-like breast cancers has spurred many research and drug development efforts. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors have shown efficacy in EGFR amplfied tumors, most notably gefitinib and erlotinib. Mutations in EGFR have been shown to confer resistance to these drugs, particularly the variant T790M, which has been functionally characterized as a resistance marker for both of these drugs. biomarkers.name: ALK
biomarkers.summary: ALK amplifications, fusions and mutations have been shown to be driving events in non-small cell lung cancer. While crizontinib has demonstrated efficacy in treating the amplification, mutations in ALK have been shown to confer resistance to current tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Second-generation TKI's have seen varied success in treating these resistant cases, and the HSP90 inhibitor 17-AAG has been shown to be cytostatic in ALK-altered cell lines.

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.summary: BRAF mutations are found to be recurrent in many cancer types. Of these, the mutation of valine 600 to glutamic acid (V600E) is the most prevalent. V600E has been determined to be an activating mutation, and cells that harbor it, along with other V600 mutations are sensitive to the BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib. It is also common to use MEK inhibition as a substitute for BRAF inhibitors, and the MEK inhibitor trametinib has seen some success in BRAF mutant melanomas. BRAF mutations have also been correlated with poor prognosis in many cancer types, although there is at least one study that questions this conclusion in papillary thyroid cancer. genes.name: BRAF
genes.description: BRAF mutations are found to be recurrent in many cancer types. Of these, the mutation of valine 600 to glutamic acid (V600E) is the most prevalent. V600E has been determined to be an activating mutation, and cells that harbor it, along with other V600 mutations are sensitive to the BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib. It is also common to use MEK inhibition as a substitute for BRAF inhibitors, and the MEK inhibitor trametinib has seen some success in BRAF mutant melanomas. BRAF mutations have also been correlated with poor prognosis in many cancer types, although there is at least one study that questions this conclusion in papillary thyroid cancer. Oncogenic BRAF mutations are divided into three cat…

biomarkers.summary: Mutations in the RAS family of proteins are frequently observed across cancer types. The amino acid positions that account for the overwhelming majority of these mutations are G12, G13 and Q61. The different protein isoforms, despite their raw similarity, also behave very differently when expressed in non-native tissue types, likely due to differences in the C-terminal hyper-variable regions. Mis-regulation of isoform expression has been shown to be a driving event in cancer, as well as missense mutations at the three hotspots previously mentioned. assertions.summary: KRAS G12C is associated with resistance to conventional cetuximab-based therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer when administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor.
KRAS G12C-positive metastatic colorectal cancer is resistant to panitumumab-based therapy when panitumumab is administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor.
KRAS A146P is associated with resistance to cetuximab in metastatic colorectal cancer (under the broader KRAS codon 146 mutation classification).
KRAS A146P is included in the broader KRAS codon 146 mutation category associated with resistance to conventional panitumumab-based therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer.
The KRAS A146P variant is likely oncogenic.
KRAS G12C is oncogenic in colorectal cancer.

biomarkers.name: HER2
biomarkers.summary: ERBB2, commonly referred to as HER2, is amplified and/or overexpressed in 20-30% of invasive breast carcinomas. HER2-positive breast cancer is treated in a separate manner from other subtypes of breast cancer and commonly presents as more aggressive disease. Metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer is now commonly treated with HER2-targeted therapy. Apart from being amplified/overexpressed, ERBB2 activating mutations have been shown to have clinical importance in HER2-negative breast cancer. These mutations have shown sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor neratinib, and highlight the importance of clinical sequencing efforts in treating breast cancer.

genes.name: ERBB2
genes.description: ERBB2, commonly referred to as HER2, is amplified and/or overexpressed in 20-30% of invasive breast carcinomas. HER2-positive breast cancer is treated in a separate manner from other subtypes of breast cancer and commonly presents as more aggressive disease. Metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer is now commonly treated with HER2-targeted therapy. Apart from being amplified/overexpressed, ERBB2 activating mutations have been shown to have clinical importance in HER2-negative breast cancer. These mutations have shown sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor neratinib, and highlight the importance of clinical sequencing efforts in treating breast cancer.

assertions.summary: HER2 amplification predicts sensitivity to Trastuzumab
HER2 amplification predicts sensitivity to Neratinib.
Breast cancers harboring ERBB2 V777L are sensitive to neratinib.
ERBB2 G292R may be sensitive to HER2 inhibitors, but data are very limited.
The ERBB2 variant G292R is of uncertain significance.
The ERBB2 V777L variant is likely oncogenic.

assertions.summary: NTRK1 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
ETV6-NTRK3–positive B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia patients can be sensitive to larotrectinib
KANK1::NTRK2 positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to larotrectinib.
EML4::NTRK3 fusion-positive solid tumors are reported to show objective response to entrectinib therapy.
ETV6::NTRK3- positive infantile fibrosarcoma tumors are sensitive to larotrectinib.
The EML4 (EMAP Like 4)::NTRK3 (Neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase) fusion is one of the diagnostic criteria for congenital (infantile) fibrosarcoma.
ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for congenital (infantile) fibrosarcoma.
ETV6::NTRK3 positive mesoblastic nephroma is responsive to larotrectinib in a pediatric case study.
NTRK2 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
NTRK3 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for the cellular subtype of congenital mesoblastic nephroma
ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for breast secretory carcinoma.
LMNA::NTRK1 is one of the diagnostic criteria for lipofibromatosis-like neural tumors (LPF-NTs).
LMNA::NTRK1 positive tumors demonstrate response to entrectinib
TPM3::NTRK1 positive solid tumors are reported to show objective response to larotrectinib therapy.
Solid tumors with TPR::NTRK1 fusion are responsive to Larotrectinib
SQSTM1::NTRK1 fusion-positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to larotrectinib.
BCR::NTRK2 fusion-positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to entrectinib.
KANK1::NTRK2 is classified as an Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
ETV6::NTRK3 is an oncogenic fusion in multiple cancer types.
SCP2::NTRK1 is classified as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion
EML4::NTRK3 is classified as an oncogenic NTRK fusion.
QKI::NTRK2 is an oncogenic fusion seen in CNS tumors.
The NTRK3::SCAPER fusion has uncertain oncogenic significance.
LMNA::NTRK1 is classified as an Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
TPR::NTRK1 Fusions are oncogenic in multiple cancer types
UFD1::NTRK2 e6::e7 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
RALGPS2::NTRK3 e1::e4 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
VPS18::NTRK3 e4::e1 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
VPS18::NTRK3 e4::e18 is classified as a NTRK fusion of uncertain significance
